gloss: member (of a group, troupe, corps, or team)

definitions.gloss: member (of a group, troupe, corps, or team)
definitions.explanation: A member of an organization whose name ends in {団|だん} — such as a musical ensemble, a theatrical company, a scout troop, a fire brigade, a delegation, or a sports supporter club. The word is general, and its specific meaning depends on what kind of {団|だん} is being discussed.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{団員|だんいん}を{募集|ぼしゅう}しています。
{彼|かれ}は{消防団|しょうぼうだん}の{団員|だんいん}です。
examples.english: He is a member of the volunteer fire brigade.

examples.japanese: {劇団|げきだん}の{団員|だんいん}たちは{毎日|まいにち}{遅|おそ}くまで{練習|れんしゅう}している。
examples.english: The members of the theater company practice every day until late.

examples.japanese: {楽団|がくだん}の{団員|だんいん}に{選|えら}ばれるためには、{厳|きび}しいオーディションに{合格|ごうかく}しなければならない。
examples.english: To be selected as a member of the orchestra, you have to pass a rigorous audition.

notes:
Composed of {団|だん} (group, troupe, body) and {員|いん} (member). Used for members of organizations whose names end in {団|だん}. The word itself is neutral about what kind of group — context or a preceding compound tells you what sort of member is meant.

USAGE:
Most commonly used in fixed compounds or paired with the specific type of group, as in {消防団員|しょうぼうだんいん} (fire brigade member), {楽団員|がくだんいん} (orchestra member), or {劇団員|げきだんいん} (theater troupe member). Standalone {団員|だんいん} generally refers back to a group that has already been mentioned.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {団員|だんいん}になる: to become a member
- {団員|だんいん}を{募集|ぼしゅう}する: to recruit members
- {団員|だんいん}{全員|ぜんいん}: all the members
- {新|しん}{団員|だんいん}: new member

RELATED TERMS:
- {消防団員|しょうぼうだんいん}: volunteer firefighter
- {楽団員|がくだんいん}: orchestra member
- {劇団員|げきだんいん}: member of a theater company
- {選手団|せんしゅだん}: team (of athletes, e.g., for the Olympics)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {会員|かいいん}: member — of a {会|かい} (association, club, society)
- {社員|しゃいん}: employee, company member — of a {会社|かいしゃ}
- {組合員|くみあいいん}: union member — of a {組合|くみあい}
- メンバー: member — general loanword, less formal
